title: Kinship template repetition audit
scope: Current public L1 one-shot DNA generation and narrative growth data.

one_shot.interpretation: Exact reconstruction of index.html dnaPool(true): 216 of 451 unique L1 DNA-button readings belong to the recursive-kinship reading set, about 47.9%.

growth.interpretation: Kinship material is not limited to one-shot generation; it is also the dominant long-tail expansion strategy.

diagnosis.structural_quality: The kinship grammar is productive and mostly grammatical.
diagnosis.product_problem: It over-concentrates public output style around 母/父 nesting, making distinct generation mechanisms feel repetitive.
diagnosis.risk: Users may perceive nominal candidate diversity as high while semantic/narrative diversity is much lower.

recommended_policy: Do not delete recursive kinship candidates or reduce the verified combinatorial space.
Throttle random one-shot DNA exposure separately from candidate inventory.
Prefer a cap around 25% for recursive kinship in the L1 DNA button as an initial product experiment.
Keep direct/manual access to recursive outputs available.
For 10-item comparison, use source/family-balanced sampling rather than uniform sampling over every materialized candidate.
For growth, stop extending every compatible family through the same mother/father long-tail; add non-kinship long-tail families before further increasing depth.
next_step: Create a one-shot DNA family exposure policy using the corrected 47.9% baseline and simulate a 25% recursive cap before changing public selection.
correction_note: v0.83 initial rough estimate used source-classified public-pool counts after seed deduplication and overstated one-shot DNA share. v0.83.1 reconstructs the actual dnaPool(true) selection pool directly. Growth statistics are unchanged.
